tools.name: check_hot_water_switch
tools.description: Use when someone asks whether a heat pump hot water system is worth it in Australia, which rebates they can stack, how much a heat pump costs after rebates, or how long it takes to pay off — including "can I combine the STC rebate with Victorian Energy Upgrades or Solar Victoria", "do I qualify", and "is a heat pump cheaper to run than gas". Given a postcode, the current hot water system and a few household facts, returns the rebates actually stackable at that postcode (with each scheme's eligibility gates and source), the net-of-rebate outlay, the payback period, and which term — rebates, the avoidable gas supply charge, the energy saving, or a replacement you were buying anyway — is really carrying the decision. Modelled estimate, not financial advice.

postcode.description: AU postcode — rebate eligibility is postcode-gated

gas_only_for_hot_water.description: true if hot water is your last gas appliance, so the daily supply charge can be avoided

replacement_due.description: true if the existing system is failing and you were replacing it anyway

owner_occupier.description: tenure — gates the means-tested state rebates

household_income.description: combined owner taxable income, for means-tested schemes (Solar Victoria caps at $150,000)

property_value.description: property value — Solar Victoria requires under $3,000,000

system_age_years.description: age of the system being replaced; Solar Victoria requires at least 3 years

building_age_years.description: age of the building; Victorian Energy Upgrades requires at least 2 years

locally_made.description: an eligible locally made unit, which raises the Victorian caps
